newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Air, GE in engine venture.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Air, GE in engine venture.

text.p: Malaysia Airlines (MAS) said on Wednesday that it and General Electric Co (GE) have set a partnership to establish an aircraft engine overhaul centre in Subang, outside the capital city.
The agreement was signed earlier today, MAS said in a statement.

Called the Aero Center of Excellence, the facility will service engines of Malaysia Airlines' fleet and of GE's Asia Pacific customers currently being serviced in the United States and Europe. It is set to begin operations in September 1997.
The joint venture company operating the centre, Aircraft Engine Repair and Overhaul (1997) Sdn Bhd, will be 70 percent owned by GE and the balance by MAS.
The venture will focus on overhauling and repairing CFM56 engines made by CFM International as well as other engine types in the MAS fleet. CFM is a 50-50 joint company of GE and Snecma of France.
MAS Chairman Tajudin Ramli said the venture would "enhance MAS operations with upgraded fleet support and improved proficiency and productivity".
MAS' contributions to the venture will be its facility and work force. GE is bringing in technology, overhaul and repair processes, management expertise and international marketing expertise.
